Disclosure  to  Promote  the  Right  To  Information 

Whereas  the  Parliament  of  India  has  set  out  to  provide  a  practical  regime  of  right  to 
information  for  citizens  to  secure  access  to  information  under  the  control  of  public  authorities, 
in  order  to  promote  transparency  and  accountability  in  the  working  of  every  public  authority, 
and  whereas  the  attached  publication  of  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  is  of  particular  interest 
to  the  public,  particularly  disadvantaged  communities  and  those  engaged  in  the  pursuit  of 
education  and  knowledge,  the  attached  public  safety  standard  is  made  available  to  promote  the 
timely  dissemination  of  this  information  in  an  accurate  manner  to  the  public. 


Mazdoor  Kisan  Shakti  Sangathan 
"The  Right  to  Information,  The  Right  to  Live''

IS  :  2319  -  1987 

Indian  Standard 

SPECIFICATION  FOR  SERGE 

(  Third  Revision  } 

0.   FOREWORD 

0.1  This  Indian  Standard  (  Third  Revision  )  was  adopted  by  the  Bureau  of 
Indian  Standards  on  6  July  1987,  after  the  draft  finalized  by  the  Wool  and 
Wool  Products  Sectional  Committee  had  been  approved  by  the  Textile 
Division  Council. 

0,2  The  standard  has  been  revised  in  the  light  of  ihe  experience  gained 
since  its  second  revision  in  1978.  In  the  present  revision,  the  following 
;aajor  changes  have  been  made: 

a)  The  requirement  for  mothproofing  has  been  modified; 

b)  The  requirement  for  wool  content  has  been  introduced; 

c)  The  ravelled  strip  test  method  has  been  prescribed  for  breaking 
strength; 

d)  The  requirement  of  staining  of  adjacent  fabric  in  case  of  colour 
fastness  to  washing  and  staining  of  solvent  in  case  of  colour  fast- 
ness to  dry  cleaning  have  been  introduced;  and 

e)  Ether  solybic  matter  (  percent )  for  varieties  No.  1,2  and  3  has 
been  modified. 

0.3  For  the  purpose  of  deciding  whether  a  particular  requirement  of  this 
standard  is  complied  with,  the  final  value,  observed  or  calculated,  express- 
ing the  result  of  a  test,  shall  be  rounded  oflF  in  accordance  uith 
IS  :  2  -  1960*.  The  number  of  significant  places  retained  in  the  rounded 
oflf  value  should  be  the  same  as  that  of  the  specified  valuejn  this  standard. 


1.  SCOPE 

1.1  This  standard  prescribes  th6  constructional    particulars  "and   other 
requirements  of  five  varieties  of  serge. 

1.2  This  standard  does  not  specify  the  indeterminable  characteristics,  like 
general  appearance,  feel,  finish  and  shade  of  cloth  (  see  also  4 ). 


*Rule$  for  rounding  off  numerical  values  (  revised ). 

3 


IS  :  2319  -  1987 

2.  MANUFACTURE 

2J  The  particulars  regarding  the  grade  of  wool  tops,  weave  and  type  of 
linish  for  the  manufacture  of  serge  are  given  in  Table  1.  The  yarn  shall 
be  spun  on  worsted  system,  except  weft  yarn  for  variety  No.  4  which  shall 
be  spun  on  woollen  system 

2.2  The  cloth  shall  be  clean,  scoured  and  free  from  grease,  soap  or  any 
other  admixture  which  might  give  it  a  fictitious  weight,  substance  or 
firmness. 

2.2.1  The  cloth  shall  have  clear-cut  finish  or  cropped  finish  as  specified 
in  Table  1. 

2.2.1.1  Clear-cut  finish  —  For  this  type  of  finish,  the  material  is  un- 
millcd  or  very  lightly  milled  and  the  surface  fibres,  particularly .  on  the  face 
side,  are  closely  cropped  by  repeated  rounds  on  shearing  machine  or  by 
singeing.  The  weave  and  texture  is  clearly  visible.  This  finish  is  commonly 
^iv(  n  to  fabrics  made  with  worsted  yarn  in  warp  and  weft. 

2.2.1.2  Cropped  finisli  —  For  this  type  of  finish,  the  material  is  milled 
;Mid  protruding  fibres  are  lightly  cropped  in  the  shearing  machine  The 
weave  and  texture  of  the  fabric  is  not  clearly  visible.  This  finish  is  com- 
!)(only  given  to  fabrics  made  with  woollen  warp  and  weft  or  with  worsted 
warp  and  voollen  weft. 

2.2.2  In  case  the  cloth  is  to  be  moth-proofed,  the  same  shall  be  render- 
ed moth-proof  by  suitable  mothproofing  chemicals  which  will  not  have 
any  toxic  effect  on  human  body.  The  manufacturer  should  declare  by 
which  chemical  the  mothproofing  has  been  done,  minimum  residual  per- 
centage of  mothproofing  chemical  in  the  fabric  and  the  suitable  method  of 
test  for  determining  the  same. 

NoTF     The  active  constituent  of  some  of  the  commonly  used   mothproofing 
chemicals  are  as  follows: 

a)  Chloro-2-chloromethyl  sulphonamidc  diphcnyl  ether  derivative  (  CCSD  ), 

b)  Halogenatcd  diphcnyl  urea  derivative,  and 

c)  2  -  Trifluromethyl  -  4  -  (  2, 4,  5  -  trichlorophcnoxy  -  5,    7  -  dichlorobenzimi- 
dazol. 

2.2.3  The  cloth  shall  be  uniformly  woven  with  firm  selvedges. 

2.2.4  The  cloth,  when  visually  examined  against  light  and  on  a  surface, 
shall  not  have  more  than  Unobjectionable  flaws  in  a  full  length  piece. 
However,  in  25  percent  of  the  pieces  in  the  lot.  up  to  a  maximum  of  16 
o!>jcctionable  flaws  per  piece  may  be  permitted.    The  objectionable  flaws

shall  be  those  which  immediately  strike  the  eyes  of  the  person  examining 
the  cloth  and  shall  be  deemed  to  include: 

a)  missing  ends  and  picks; 

b)  flats; 

c)  cuts  and  holes; 

d)  stains; 

e)  weft  bars  and  warp  section  marks; 

f )  big  stubs,  knots  and  specks; 

g)  prominently  noticeable  thick  and  thin  places;  and 
h)  dyeing  defects  (  streaks,  patches,  etc  ). 

2.2.4.1  All  objectionable  flaws  shall  be  marked  by  means  of  a  thread 
of  a  contrasting  shade  sewn  in  the  selvedge  opposite  the  flaw.  An  allow- 
ance of  10  cm  shall  be  given  for  each  flaw  up  to  12  flaws  in  the  piece. 
However,  in  case  of  pieces  having  flaws  exceeding  12  and  up  to  16,  an 
allowance  of  25  cm  for  each  such  flaw  shall  be  given. 

2.2.4.2  A  reference  may  be  made  to  IS  :  4125  -  1987*  for  details  of 
these  flaws. 

3.  REQUIREMENTS 

3.1  The  constructional  particulars  of  the  five  varieties  of  serge  shall  con- 
form to  those  given  in  Table  2. 

3.2  The  other  requirements  of  cloth  shall  conform  to  those  given  in 
Table  3. 

4.  SEALED  SAMPLE 

4.1  If,  in  order  to  illustrate  or  specify  the  general  appearance,  feci,  shade, 
finish,  etc,  of  cloth,  a  sample  has  been  agreed  upon  and  scaled,  the  supply 
siiall  be  in  conformity  with  the  sample  in  such  respects. 

4.1.1  The  custody  of  the  sealed  sample  shall  be  a  matter  of  prior  agrce- 
iJtcnt  between  the  buyer  and  the  seller. 

f .  MARKING 

!  .1  The  cloth  shall  be  marked  with  the  following: 
a)  Name  of  the  material;

5AA  The  cloth  may  also  be  marked  with  the  Standard  Majk. 

NoTi;  —  The  use  of  the  Standard  Mark  is  governed  by  the  provisions  of  the 
Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  Act,  1986  and  the  Rules  and  Regulations  made  there- 
under. The  BIS  Mark  on  products  covered  by  an  Indian  Standard  con\eys  the 
assurance  that  they  have  been  produced  to  comply  '  ith  the  requirenvnts  of  that 
Standard  under  a  well-defined  system  of  inspection,  testing  and  quality  control  which 


*G.uide  for  marking  textile  materials  made  of  wool  ( first  revision  ).

is  devised  and  supervised  by  BIS  and  operated  by  the  producer.  BIS  marked  pro- 
ducts are  also  continuously  checked  by  BIS  for  conformity  to  that  standard  as  a 
further  safeguard.  Details  of  conditions  under  which  a  licence  for  the  use  of  the 
Standard  Mark  may  be  granted  to  manufacturers  or  processors,  may  be  obtained 
from  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards.

6.  PRESERVATION 


6.1  If  the  cloth  has  not  been  rendered  moth-proof,  the  same  shall  be 
packed  with  a  heavy  dose  of  napthalene,  that  is,  with  a  minimum  quantity 
of  five  kilograms  per  cubic  metre  of  the  volume  of  the  bale  or  case. 


18:2319-1987 

7.  PACKING 

7.1  The  cloth  shall  be  packed  in  bales  or  cases  in  conformity  with  the 
procedure  laid  down  either  in  IS  :  32  -  1971*  or  in  IS  :  741  -  1971t,  as 
required. 

7.2  Alternatively,  the  cloth  may  be  packed  according  to  the  details  given, 
when  specifically  agreed  to  between  the  buyer  and  the  seller. 

Each  cloth  piece  shall  be  suitably  folded  in  a  rectangular  form  or 
wrapped  on  cardboard  or  strawboard  of  suitable  size  and  thickness.  Each 
piece  shall  then  be  wrapped  with  polyethylene  film  of  minimum  40  micron 
thickness  or  alternatively  kraft  paper.  The  edges  of  the  kraft  paper  or 
polyethylene  film  shall  be  gummed  or  sealed.  Alternatively,  each  piece 
may  be  tied  with  twine  at  least  at  two  places.  Such  pieces,  in  a  suitable 
number,  shall  then  be  enclosed  in  a  layer  of  heavy  cee  jute  cloth,  preferably 
conforming  to  IS  :  3751  -  1966t,  to  form  compact  bales.  The  bales  shall 
be  made  secure  by  cross  hooping  the  steel  strips  at  right  angles  to  both 
the  length  and  the  width  of  the  bale.  The  gross  mass  of  the  bale  shall  not 
normally  exceed  200  kg.  All  packing  materials  shall  conform  to 
IS  :  741  1971t. 

8.  SAMPLING  AND  CRITERIA  FOR  CONFORMITY 

8.1  Lot  —  The  quantity  of  cloth  delivered  to  one  buyer  against  one  des- 
patch note  shall  constitute  a  lot. 

8.2  The  conformity  of  a  lot  to  the  requirement  of  the  standard  shall  be 
determined  on  the  basis  of  the  tests  carried  out  on  the  samples  selected 
from  the  lot. 

8.3  Unless  otherwise  agreed  between  the  buyer  and  the  seller,  the  number 
of  pieces  to  be  selected  at  random  shall  be  in  accordance  with  col  1  and 
2  of  Table  4.  To  ensure  randomness  of  selection,  IS  :  4905  -  1968§  may 
be  used. 


♦Codeforscaworthy  packaging  of  woollen  and  worsted  yarn,  and  cloth  {second 
revision  ). 

tCodc  for  inland  packaging  of  woollen  and  worsted  yarn,  and  cloth  {first 
revision  ). 

{Specification  for  heavy  cee  cloth. 

§Methods  of  random  sampling.

APPENDIX    A 

(Table  2) 

METHOD  FOR  DETERMINATION  OF  BREAKING  STRENGTH 

A-1.  CONDITIONING 

A-U  Prior  to  test,  the  test  specimens  shall  be  conditioned  for  at  least  24 
hours  in  standard  atmosphere  of  65  ±  2  percent  relative  humidity  and 
27  ±  2"C  ( see  also  IS  :  6359  -  1971*  ). 

A-1 .2  The  tests  shall  also  be  carried  out  in  standard  atmosphere 
(  see  A-1.1 ). 


*Method  for  conditioning  of  textiles. 


12 


IS  :  2319  .  1987 
A-2.  PREPARATION  OF  TEST  SPECIMEN 

A-2.1  For  the  purpose  of  this  test,  the  test  specimens  of  size  300  x 
200  mm  shall  be  cut  in  both  warpway  and  weftway  directions  from  each 
of  the  sample  pieces  as  selected  in  col  4  of  Table  4.  The  preparation  of 
the  ravelled  strip  test  specimens  shall  be  done  according  to  9  of 
IS:  1969-  1985*. 

A-3.  TESTING  APPARATUS 

A-3.1  The  requirements  of  the  tensile  strength  testing  machine  shall  be 
according  to  7  of  IS  :  1969  -  1985  V 

A-4.  JAW  FACES  AND  MOUNTING  OF  THE  TEST  SPECIMEN 

A-4.1  The  width  of  the  jaw  faces  of  the  tensile  testing  machine  shall  be  at 
least  170  mm.  The  mounting  of  the  test  specimens  shall  be  according  to 
8,23  of  IS  :1%9- 1985*. 

A-5.  TEST  PROCEDURE 

A-5.1  The  test  procedure  shall  be  according  to  11  of  IS  :  1969  -  1985*. 

A-^.  CALCULATIONS  AND  REPORTING 

A-6.1  The  calculations  for  breaking  strength  shall  be  done  according  to  11 
of  IS:  1969-  1985*. 


APPENDIX   B 

(  Table  3  ) 

DROP  TEST 

B-1.  TEST  SPECIMENS 

ft-l.l  Draw  test  specimens  from  the  test  sample  (  see  8.3  )>  each  measur- 
iag  20  X  25  cm  from  each  piece  in  the  sample  under  test. 


''Method  for  determination  of  breaking  load  and  elongation  of  woven  textile 
fiibrics  (  u^MMkd  revision  ). 

13 


IS  :  2319  .  1987 

B-2.  PROCEDURE 

B-2.1  Clamp  one  test  specimen  on  a  transparent  glass  plate  inclined  at  an 
angle  of  45**.  Allow  water  to  drop  from  a  glass  jet  on  the  face  of  the  test 
specimen  from  a  height  of  two  metres  at  the  rate  of  18  drops  per  minute, 
adjusting  the  size  of  the  jet  and  the  flow  of  water  so  that  18  d=  1  drops 
of  water  representing  a  volume  of  1  ±  005  ml  are  discharged  every 
minute. 

B-2.2  During  30  minutes  from  the  start  of  the  test,  examine  from  time  to 
time  the  back  of  the  test  specimen  without  disturbing  it,  and  observe 
whether  water  penetrates  through  the  test  specimen  or  not. 

B-2.3  Repeat  the  test  with  the  remaining  test  specimens.
